subject: Delayed token emission — short-term client fixes & canary rollout
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@orchidai.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-31T18:05:00-08:00
Subject: Delayed token emission — short-term client fixes & canary rollout

Hi Samira —

Thanks for flagging the slow streaming behavior you saw in the Morning PDT peak. We investigated and have identified a pattern where some live chat requests encounter delayed token emission (slow first-byte for streaming) when the conversation seed includes long system instructions + a large recent-activity KV cache.

Top-line: we have a short-term mitigation you can apply in-app today and a safe canary rollout schedule we can run on your Dedicated pool to confirm the longer-term fix.

Immediate actions (suggested):
- Reduce "system" prompt size for streaming sessions to <= 600 tokens where feasible. This lowers initial KV expansion and avoids slow first-token synthesis.
- If you control the client retry, set a 3s initial chunk timeout and retry with an increased backoff — this prevents duplicate completions while giving the model time to emit the first chunk.
- Toggle conversation_prefix_cache=false in your SDK call for sessions that rehydrate large context repeatedly (this trades cost for lower latency).

We'll also run a restricted canary on a subset of your Dedicated nodes to deploy a kernel-level pacing adjustment that reduces token emission stalls. Proposed canary schedule attached (proposed-canary-schedule.xlsx).

Attached: diagnostic_snapshot_20261101.log (trimmed) and a sanitized client payload we used for repro.

I will follow up with a short-runbook for your engineering team to test the client-side toggles.

— Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
Jonas Weber
Redwood Inference

Jonas — quick internal note for the triage/ops thread:

We've confirmed the repro traces in SRE ticket SRE-4821 show two correlated factors:
1) Large system prompts cause extended KV deserialization on the serving path for certain quantized kernels.
2) When a session rehydrates a deep KV cache (many recent messages + embeddings), our prefix scheduling sometimes delays first-chunk emission while rebalancing attention memory.

Short-term plan (WE own):
- Ops: schedule the pacing kernel tweak as a staged canary (rollout window: Nov 2, 02:00–06:00 UTC) limited to 10% of OrchidAI traffic.
- Solutions (Jonas/Marissa): provide an SDK snippet and a checklist for Orchids on how to safely toggle conversation_prefix_cache and set chunk timeout/backoff. Add note about cost trade-off.
- CSM: notify account and confirm the maintenance window and that SLA metrics will not be downgraded (we'll monitor KPIs closely).

I'll prepare the short postmortem template after the canary completes; include the trimmed logs in the SRE ticket.

— Laura
Director, Customer Reliability

(Attachment: client_request_payload.json)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@orchidai.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Delayed token emission — short-term client fixes & canary rollout

Hi Samira — quick update after the canary window: we deployed the kernel pacing adjustment to 10% of your Dedicated capacity during the scheduled window and instrumented a live metric to track first-byte latency for streaming. Results:

- Average first-chunk latency for affected sessions dropped from ~1.8s to ~0.45s in the canary cohort.
- No increase in error rates or token duplication observed.
- Customer-visible cost impact from toggling conversation_prefix_cache=false is measurable (~6–9% more tokens billed on heavy-history sessions) — we included that note in the attached checklist.

Suggested next steps for OrchidAI:
1) Apply the client-side change (3s chunk timeout + exponential backoff) to all web clients this week.
2) Consider reducing system prompt verbosity where possible; our SDK example includes an automated truncation utility you can adopt.
3) If you want us to proceed, we'll schedule a gradual rollout of the kernel adjustment to 50% over the next two weeks and monitor latency and cost KPIs.

If you approve, I'll open a change request and include the full postmortem write-up and the SRE trace links (SRE-4821) once we finalize.

Thanks for the quick coordination — appreciate the help getting this verified.

— Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
